_comment: The DPG-23 candidate shortlist, as DATA so that widening it is an edit, not a redesign.
That matters because the licence limb of the filter is PROVISIONAL: Q-04-02 asks whether
restricted-use open weights (Llama, Gemma class) count as open alternatives for indicator 4. If
the answer loosens, move rows from `excluded` to `shortlist` and re-run — no code changes.
The filter, from 03-open-models-spec.md: permissive licence (Apache-2.0 / MIT) · real
multilingual coverage including Nepali · reliable guided decoding · fits one 24 GB GPU at 4-bit.
Catalogue read from https://router.huggingface.co/v1/models on 2026-08-20 (132 models served).
Licences are VERIFIED AT RUN TIME from each model card, never from this file — see llm_smoke.py.

shortlist.why: The incumbent placeholder in .env.open, so it has to be measured rather than assumed. Cheapest serious candidate, eight providers on the router, and the only one that comfortably fits well under the 24 GB limb. Reasoning model — watch the token cap.
shortlist.measured_2026_08_20: ✅ All six capabilities. `json_schema` honoured (proved, not assumed). 0.73s on the probe — 30x faster than the Qwen family, which matters because latency here is pass/fail against the interactive budget, not a table row.

shortlist.why: The bigger sibling, and the .env.open placeholder for translation and SEAH findings before Q-21 collapsed the template to two models. Included to measure what that split would have bought. FAILS the 24 GB limb — relevant only while T2 stays parked and inference is hosted.
The strongest multilingual coverage available under a permissive licence, and dense-27B is the size the spec's candidate table names for classification and summary. Fits 24 GB at 4-bit.
Same family, MoE — tests whether a similar quality tier is reachable at materially lower inference cost, which is the trade the spec's candidate table explicitly asks about.

The cheap-and-fast end. Q-11 notes per-task downsizing became MORE attractive once T2 was parked (there is no paid-for GPU whose capacity is already sunk), and extraction is schema-constrained work where guided decoding does most of the job.
shortlist.measured_2026_08_20: ⚠ Accepts `json_schema` and does NOT honour it — 200, well-formed JSON, none of the required fields. Pinned to `json_object` in _PROFILES. Also the slowest probe measured (23.8s on one sentence), which is a serious risk against a 30s interactive budget.

shortlist.why: The strongest DPG story in the list: fully open weights AND open training data, built explicitly for low-resource language coverage. If it is competitive on Nepali it is the most defensible choice on indicator 4, not merely an acceptable one. FAILS the 24 GB limb at 70B.
shortlist.measured_2026_08_20: ⚠ PROVISIONALLY OUT. Its only reply to the probe was 'Your request was blocked' — a content filter, in 0.42s, on a grievance about children falling ill from construction dust. Kept in the SHORTLIST rather than moved to `excluded` on purpose: it is not yet established whether the filter belongs to the model or to the serving provider, and if it is the provider's then another route to the same weights has no such problem. See followups/apertus-content-filter-blocks-a-grievance.md.

shortlist.why: MIT, small, and a useful floor: if a 14B model is adequate on this taxonomy, the cost conversation with the Nepal Government changes shape. Weak multilingual coverage is the expected failure — worth measuring rather than assuming.

excluded.reason: Bespoke community licence with use restrictions. Excluded by the PROVISIONAL licence limb, not on quality — Gemma-class models are among the strongest multilingual options at this size, so this exclusion may be costing real Nepali quality. Q-04-02.
Same. Named separately because it is the exact size class the spec's candidate table recommends.
Llama Community License — use restrictions and an acceptable-use policy. Same provisional exclusion. Q-04-02.

⚠ The exclusion that hurts most. Aya is PURPOSE-BUILT for multilingual coverage and is exactly the right size, but CC-BY-NC forbids commercial use — and unlike the Gemma/Llama limb this one does NOT loosen if Q-04-02 loosens, because non-commercial is incompatible with a government production deployment however indicator 4 is read. Excluded on licence, not on quality.
Inherits Gemma terms. Also: SEA-LION targets South-EAST Asian languages; Nepali is South Asian and is not in its focus set, so the regional-specialist argument does not apply here.

Licence is fine. Excluded on SIZE — 106B total is far outside the 24 GB limb, and the family's smaller members are not on the router. Kept in the record so a later reader knows it was considered rather than missed.

asr.why: The .env.open placeholder, and whisper-1 IS Whisper — so this is close to a drop-in for a closed dependency that was never actually live here.
asr.measured_2026_08_20: ✅ Licence apache-2.0, verified from the model card — the expectation held. ⚠ WER unmeasured: the benchmark set has no audio, and .env.open's ASR endpoint 404s (D-53).

asr.why: 14.76% Nepali WER in the 2026 OpenSLR SLR54 comparative study — best-equal, and faster than large-v3.
asr.measured_2026_08_20: ⚠ Licence is MIT, NOT apache-2.0 — the expectation above was wrong, and so was DPG-22's table until 2026-08-27. Both pass the permissive filter so no decision changes, but do not repeat the apache-2.0 claim. ⚠ WER unmeasured, same two blockers as large-v3.
